notes: Feng Office SQL injection in MoreController update_system_module_order/update_dimension_order via modules/dims argument. No poc_refs; the only PoC is a Google Drive PDF that cannot be fetched, and no accessible source gives the concrete URL path or request shape. Feng Office uses an index.php?c=<controller>&a=<action> routing convention, but the exact route for MoreController could not be confirmed, so building would require guessing the path. Per spec, dropped rather than invent an endpoint.

Feng Office SQL injection in Legacy API Contacts::instance->findAll (CompanyWebsite.class.php) via auth argument. No poc_refs; the only PoC is a Google Drive PDF that cannot be fetched. No accessible source gives the concrete URL path/route or request shape for the legacy API 'auth' parameter, so building would require guessing the endpoint. Per spec, dropped rather than invent an endpoint.

SQL injection in OpenPanel analytics filter builder via a profile.* filter column identifier. The GHSA/VulnCheck advisories name the entry path (GET /insights/:projectId/events and sibling insights endpoints) but deliberately withhold any PoC and do not document how analytics filters are serialized onto the request (query string vs JSON body, exact filter-object encoding). The injection is in a column identifier inside a filter 'name' field; building a faithful request would require guessing the request encoding, so dropped per spec.

NoSQL injection (CWE-943) in the MongoDB integration for Laravel: the three-argument where method with '='/'eq', and the find/delete methods on that path, can interpret an operator-shaped array as a query condition. This is a library-level flaw with no fixed HTTP endpoint or parameter; exploitation depends entirely on how a consuming application wires user input into these APIs. No concrete path+parameter to target, so no faithful WAF request can be built.

Unauthenticated SQL injection in the Yo WordPress plugin (<=1.3.1) via the username request parameter. WPScan and Wordfence both withhold the PoC ('displayed once remediated'), and neither the advisories nor plugin searches reveal the exact endpoint (AJAX action name / admin-ajax.php action / REST route) carrying the username parameter. Parameter name alone (username) is insufficient; building would require guessing the path/action, so dropped.

Unauthenticated SQL injection in the Tz Weekly Radio Schedule WordPress plugin (tz-wrs-core <=1.8.1) via an AJAX action. The WPScan PoC is withheld; the vulnerability name references the action tzwrs_update_cell, but the exact injectable parameter name is not published and could not be recovered (plugin SVN trunk listings redirect to http and did not resolve). Guessing the parameter would fail condition 2, so dropped.

Tz Weekly Radio Schedule WordPress plugin (tz-wrs-core) <=1.8.1 unauthenticated SQLi on an AJAX action. WPScan PoC is withheld ('displayed once remediated', no known fix) and names no AJAX action; the WPScan title hints the 'week' parameter but the admin-ajax.php action is not disclosed. Wordfence page is JS-rendered (no extractable detail) and plugin SVN source is unreachable via the agent proxy. Cannot determine the exact action without guessing, so condition 2 fails.

Product Question and Answer WordPress plugin <=1.1.0 unauthenticated SQLi on AJAX actions. WPScan PoC withheld; neither the AJAX action name nor the exact parameter is disclosed. Wordfence page is JS-rendered and plugin SVN source is unreachable via the agent proxy. Building a faithful admin-ajax.php request would require guessing the action/parameter, so condition 2 fails.

Price Drop Alert for WooCommerce WordPress plugin (woo-price-drop-alert) <=1.1 unauthenticated SQLi on an AJAX action. WPScan PoC withheld; no AJAX action name or parameter disclosed. Wordfence/Sentinelone pages carry no request detail and plugin SVN source is unreachable via the agent proxy. Cannot build without guessing the action/parameter, so condition 2 fails.

'wp shortcut link and advertisement baner' WordPress plugin <=1.2.0 unauthenticated SQLi on an AJAX action. WPScan PoC withheld; no AJAX action name or parameter disclosed. No Wordfence/threat-intel page with request detail located and plugin SVN source is unreachable via the agent proxy. Cannot build without guessing the action/parameter, so condition 2 fails.

SQL injection lives in the llmware Python library's collection-database layer (llmware/resources.py). The tainted filter/lookup values reach the sink only through in-process Python API calls (Library.block_lookup, Query.text_query_with_custom_filter, Query.text_query_by_author_or_speaker); llmware ships no HTTP server exposing these, so there is no inbound server-side HTTP request to simulate. Per SPEC 3.4, library/Python API injections are dropped.

n8n Elasticsearch/Firestore query injection is a workflow node EXPRESSION injection (PR:L, attacker edits a workflow). The advisory names no inbound HTTP route, path or parameter against n8n itself; the malicious value is interpolated inside a node's query field, not sent as a WAF-inspectable request. No faithful server-side HTTP request can be built.

AVideo get.json.php APIName=channels sort injection is an ORDER BY identifier/column oracle: the endpoint's character filter strips quotes, parentheses and commas, so only bare identifiers like u.password pass. The faithful exploit payload (a column name) carries no WAF-detectable attack signature, and any classic SQLi signature would not match the real (filtered) attack. Fails condition 1.

MikroORM is a Node.js/TypeScript ORM library. The orderBy direction SQL injection occurs inside em.find()/QueryBuilder.orderBy() when an application binds attacker input to the direction value. There is no fixed HTTP path or parameter - it depends entirely on the consuming application. No faithful CVE-specific request can be built without guessing an endpoint.

Kirki WordPress plugin (6.0.0-6.2.5) Editor+ SQL injection via a 'Content Manager Field ID' identifier. WPScan withheld the PoC and neither WPScan, Wordfence, Patchstack nor the Lutra field guide disclose the concrete endpoint (admin-ajax action or REST route), parameter name, or payload. Building would require guessing the path/parameter, which the spec forbids.
waf_rules_found: Wordfence and Patchstack advisories indicate generic SQLi mitigation rules exist but neither publishes the request path/parameter.

notes: wp-review-slider-pro < 12.7.12 stored SQLi via an AJAX handler lacking a capability check. The WPScan PoC is withheld ('displayed once remediated') and neither the Wordfence entry, OpenCVE nor the CVE record names the exact parameter or AJAX action. Only a 'Stored Template Filter' hint is given. Cannot determine the exact parameter/action without guessing, so dropped per spec condition 2.

NextGen Connect (Mirth Connect) <=4.7.1: an authenticated user can execute arbitrary SQL through the Database Connector API. This is abuse of a feature that legitimately sends SQL to connected databases, not injection via a specific request parameter. No advisory/PoC/WAF rule gives a concrete inbound HTTP path, parameter, and injectable payload, so no faithful CVE-tied, signature-bearing request can be built. The securityarsenal guide only offers generic SQLi detection heuristics (UNION SELECT / SLEEP( on /api/, /webadmin/, /services/mirth), not an exploit-derived request.

ILIAS repository trash table SQL injection via the table navigation sort field (ORDER BY). The VulnCheck advisory and the researcher advisory (SIT-2026-001) explicitly state they contain no ready-to-use PoC and no payloads. Only the value format 'field:direction:offset' is given; the exact HTTP parameter name, the baseClass/cmdClass/cmd route, and the trash-table GET parameter name are not published. Building a request would require guessing the parameter name, which the spec forbids.

WPvivid Backup, Migration & Staging < 0.9.133 admin SQL injection via an unsanitised user-supplied list of identifiers. The WPScan advisory withholds the PoC and does not name the vulnerable AJAX action/endpoint or the exact parameter. No other source (fieldguide, opencve, hol.org) names a concrete path+parameter. Admin-only, medium severity. Building would require guessing the parameter, which the spec forbids.

IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 SQLi in the Analytic Grid Service Handler (analytic cases grid endpoint). Closed-source enterprise product; only an IBM bulletin exists, naming the component but giving no concrete URL path, parameter name, HTTP method, or PoC. Cannot build a faithful request without inventing the endpoint/parameter.

Mislabeled as SQLi; actually stored DOM-based XSS in Concrete CMS Gallery block per-image Caption field. The caption is attribute-encoded on storage and only executes client-side when the Magnific Popup lightbox re-parses it via jQuery .append() (titleSrc). No public PoC or documented storing endpoint/parameter for the block-edit request; only vendor release notes. Payload is not present as raw HTML in an inbound request, so no WAF-blockable server-side signature could be built faithfully.

IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 SQLi in the New Query Builder REST Processor (newQueryBuilder REST endpoint). Closed-source; only the IBM bulletin exists, naming the processor but giving no concrete URL path, injectable parameter, method, or PoC. Cannot build without guessing.

IBM Guardium Data Protection 12.2 unauthenticated SQLi in the Load Balancer Groups component (Load Balancer Servlet / LBServlet). Closed-source; IBM bulletin and third-party write-ups mention 'LBServlet' but give no concrete path, injectable parameter name, method, or PoC request. Cannot build a faithful request without inventing the parameter.

MongoDB PHP client library (mongo-php-library / mongo-php-driver) does not sanitize application-supplied namespace identifiers. This is a library-level flaw: it only manifests if an application passes untrusted text into namespace identifiers. No defined inbound HTTP endpoint, path, or request parameter exists to target, and no attack-signature payload applies. Not a server-side inbound HTTP request.

Craft CMS GraphQL entry mutation (saveEntry/deleteEntry) reads siteId without site-scope filtering, letting a token scoped to Site A act on Site B. Mislabeled as SQL injection; it is an authorization/site-scope bypass. The exploit only passes a normal integer siteId in a GraphQL mutation - there is no malicious attack signature (no SQLi/XSS/traversal payload) that a WAF would block. Fails condition 1.

CakePHP framework library flaw: FunctionsBuilder::cast/extract/datePart/dateAdd in src/Database/FunctionsBuilder.php accept user-controlled dataType/part/unit and incorporate them as unescaped SQL fragments. This is a framework API issue that only manifests if an application passes untrusted input to these builder methods. No defined inbound HTTP endpoint, path, or parameter. Not a server-side inbound HTTP request.

WP Ultimate CSV Importer SQL injection requires an authenticated administrator to upload a CSV whose cell (mapped to the All in One SEO seo_title field) contains a SQL subquery. The injection lives inside an uploaded CSV file processed through the multi-step admin import wizard; no concrete single HTTP endpoint/path or request parameter is documented, and CRS/ModSecurity does not inspect uploaded file contents by default. Cannot faithfully reconstruct one inbound request with a named parameter; fails condition 2.

ash_sql is an Elixir library (AshSql.Expr). The bug is a self-defeating LIKE-wildcard escape helper reached through contains/2, string_starts_with/2, string_ends_with/2 - a library API, not a specific inbound HTTP endpoint/parameter. The value stays parameterized (confined to LIKE pattern grammar, not full SQL), so there is no real SQL-injection signature to place and no concrete path+parameter. CWE-943 but not expressible as a WAF-blockable web request.

WP Project Manager Pro (wedevs) authenticated subscriber SQL injection. No public PoC available (SentinelOne: 'No verified public proof-of-concept code is available'). Wordfence advisory page returns empty content and names no parameter; NVD/OpenCVE give no concrete endpoint or vulnerable parameter. Advisory only says 'user-supplied parameter' used in an AJAX/REST query. Cannot determine exact path+parameter without guessing, so dropped per spec section 5.

ash_sqlite is an Elixir/Ash data-layer library. The flaw is in AshSqlite.SqlImplementation building a SQLite json_extract path from a get_path/2 segment; the path is bound as a parameter and the issue is confined to the JSON-path grammar (not SQL injection). No concrete server-side HTTP endpoint or parameter exists - exploitability depends entirely on an unknown consuming application's 'pick-a-field' endpoint. Library-level, no fixed path/parameter to build a faithful request. Advisory itself says this is not SQL but JSON-path traversal.

CakePHP framework-level issue: FunctionsBuilder::jsonValue() with PostgresDriver is injectable when user data reaches the jsonPath argument. This is a PHP framework API, not a concrete inbound HTTP request - there is no fixed path or request parameter. Exploitability depends on an unknown application passing user input into jsonValue(). No path/parameter to build a request tied to the CVE.

The authoritative PoC gist describes a CWE-20 array-coercion input-validation bug in POST /public/submit.php (person[0][]=...), NOT SQL injection: the insert uses a prepared statement with bind_param('s', $person) and a nested array is coerced to the literal string 'Array' and stored. No 'Researcher' parameter and no injectable SQL signature exist. CWE-89 over-labels the bug; trusting the PoC there is no attack signature a WAF would/should block.

WordPress egoi Smart Marketing plugin 'SQL injection via Parameter Name'. The vulnerable listener (class-egoi-for-wp-listener.php) is not a dedicated plugin endpoint; it is invoked via init($user_id) from an internal WordPress hook (user registration / profile / WooCommerce checkout) and merges all $_POST keys (array_merge($_POST,...)) into a query via get_default_map(). The injection is in the parameter NAME, not value, and no public source identifies the exact HTTP endpoint/URL that triggers it. Wordfence advisory page returned empty; trac is robots-disallowed. Building would require guessing the trigger endpoint, which the spec forbids.

TYPO3 extension 'Forms Export' (frp_form_answers / frappant) SQL injection in a backend module. The advisory does not name the injectable URL parameter, the backend module route, or the HTTP method, and no public PoC exists. TYPO3 backend modules require an authenticated backend session and a valid module route token, so the exact path+parameter cannot be reconstructed from public sources. Entry point not recoverable.

n8n Supabase node PostgREST filter injection. This is a workflow-node configuration/expression-resolution issue, not an inbound HTTP request to a fixed n8n endpoint. The GHSA advisory names no HTTP path, parameter, or request format; exploitation depends on a workflow routing untrusted input (e.g. via a webhook trigger) into a manual-filter Supabase operation. No concrete path+parameter to tie a WAF request to the CVE.

n8n MongoDB node NoSQL injection ($ne/$where via resolved Query expression). This is a workflow-node configuration/expression-resolution issue, not an inbound HTTP request to a fixed n8n endpoint. The GHSA advisory names no HTTP path or parameter; exploitation depends on a workflow placing externally-controlled data into the MongoDB node Query field. No concrete path+parameter to tie a WAF request to the CVE.

GeoTools is a Java geospatial library. SQLi is in the jsonArrayContains OGC filter function (PostGIS DataStore). The advisory, PR and commit give no concrete HTTP request, endpoint path or parameter; GeoTools itself exposes no HTTP surface. Reaching it would require guessing a GeoServer WFS/CQL_FILTER endpoint, which the spec forbids.

baserCMS SQLi in BcDatabaseService.php is triggered through a multi-step backup-restore chain: the attacker plants malicious table names via a schema-file ZIP uploaded during restore, then error-based SQLi fires on later operations. The VulnCheck advisory gives no single HTTP request with an injectable parameter and value; the only direct-POST point (deleteTables schema) has no confirmed endpoint/parameter. Not expressible as one inbound request with a signature in a named parameter.

Fabrik (Joomla extension) unauthenticated SQLi in the list ORDER BY via an 'order' parameter with a CONCAT( allowlist bypass. No public PoC; advisories name the attack class but not the exact Joomla request structure (com_fabrik list view id, how the order var is packaged in the request). Building would require guessing the parameter packaging and listid, which the spec forbids.

Fabrik (Joomla extension) unauthenticated SQLi in the list filter 'condition' parameter concatenated into the WHERE clause (getFilterQuery). No public PoC; advisories give no concrete HTTP request, no com_fabrik list id and no exact request-var naming for the condition parameter. Exact entry point cannot be reconstructed without guessing.

WP Import Export Lite < 3.9.33 SQLi via export filter values. WPScan advisory withholds the PoC (scheduled for 2026-09-28) and gives no endpoint, parameter name or payload. Unlike its sibling CVE-2026-76557 (import), no entry point is public, so it cannot be tied to a concrete parameter without guessing.
Cisco ISE API SQLi; vendor PSIRT advisory names no concrete endpoint path or parameter, no PoC. Cannot build a CVE-tied request.
Splunk SOAR SQLi via custom function results / DB lookup name; advisory gives no REST endpoint path or parameter, no PoC.
Splunk Enterprise Data Orchestration jobs SQLi; advisory (SVD-2026-0801) names no concrete REST path or parameter, no PoC.
Splunk Enterprise SPL injection via saved-search dispatch time values; no concrete path/parameter in advisory and SPL is not a standard WAF signature class.
stigmem-node Postgres schema-identifier SQLi is an internal/library code path; schema value is operator-controlled from deployment config, not an inbound HTTP parameter. No endpoint.

Marten is a .NET document-DB/ORM library. The SQL injection is in internal LINQ/tenant-management code paths (DictionaryItemMember.cs, SelectParser.cs, DatabaseScopedTenantPartitions.cs, etc.) reached via library API calls such as Where filters and IEventStore.DeleteProjectionProgressAsync. There is no fixed inbound HTTP endpoint or request parameter; the tainted input is a dictionary indexer key supplied through the .NET API, not an HTTP request. Not expressible as a WAF webRequest.

GraphQL query injection in the Rapid7 Bulk Export MCP server (get_export_status, export_manager.py). The injectable export_id arrives as an MCP tool argument from an MCP client (or indirect prompt injection), not as an inbound HTTP request to the vulnerable component; the resulting GraphQL document is sent OUTBOUND to Rapid7's API under the operator's own API key. There is no server-side inbound HTTP endpoint/parameter a WAF could inspect, and it grants no access beyond the operator's existing authenticated scope.

Library-level NoSQL/aggregation-expression injection in the MongoDB-for-Laravel cache lock implementation: a caller-supplied lock 'owner' value is evaluated as an aggregation expression. The owner value is set by the consuming application's own code (Laravel cache lock API), so there is no fixed HTTP endpoint, path or request parameter to target; the vector depends entirely on how a downstream app wires user input into the lock owner. No public PoC request, path or parameter. label_confidence was low.

Authenticated Contao-backend SQL injection in several Isotope eCommerce backend callbacks (Attribute/Callback.php onLoad/validateForeignKey, ProductPrice/Callback.php, MediaManager.php) that interpolate request-controlled identifiers and admin-supplied values. The VulnCheck advisory and GitHub issue #2585 intentionally omit a weaponized PoC and do not pin the concrete backend route (the Contao do= module) or request parameter; building a faithful request would require guessing the backend module path and parameter. Per spec, dropped rather than guess the entry point.

SQL injection is triggered via a crafted SIP From header (Caller ID name) on an inbound SIP call to a monitored extension, inserted by agi-bin/missedcallnotify.php. It is not reachable by an inbound HTTP request, so no webRequest can simulate it.

SQLi is delivered through a crafted MySQL table NAME (backtick + stacked statement) that executes when a Budibase admin later runs schema discovery (DESCRIBE). The injection payload lives in a database object name, not in any parameter of the triggering inbound HTTP request, so there is no WAF-inspectable attack signature on the wire.

Advisory (GHSA-q6x4-v3qx-85qw) describes MySQL multipleStatements:true but its only PoC is a Node.js mysql2 script connecting directly to the database. No HTTP endpoint, path or request parameter is named, and the description only says 'user input fields' generically. Cannot tie a payload to a concrete inbound request.

PeerTube SQLi in ActorFollowModel.updateScore via actor inboxUrl. The injected value (inboxUrl) is read from a remote ActivityPub actor document that PeerTube fetches server-side during federation, not supplied in a WAF-inspectable parameter of the inbound inbox/follow request. Fix commit confirms inboxUrl string interpolation but no inbound HTTP parameter carries the payload.

ERPNext SQLi sink is get_tax_template(posting_date, args) in tax_rule.py, confirmed string-interpolating posting_date into a WHERE clause. But get_tax_template is NOT @frappe.whitelist() (verified in source); it is only reached internally. No advisory/PoC names the whitelisted HTTP endpoint and parameter that carry attacker-controlled posting_date, so building a request would require inventing the entry point.

Metabase SQLi via a public card/dashboard field-filter (dimension) parameter. The GHSA advisory gives no endpoint path, no card/dashboard UUID handling and no field-filter parameter name, and no public PoC exists. Cannot place a payload in a confirmed path+parameter.

Metabase SQLi via POST /api/session/reset_password is known at endpoint level, but the root cause (per Bishop Fox / VulnCheck) is failure to restrict UNDECLARED fields in the reset body, not classic string concatenation, and the specific injectable field name is not public (no PoC released). Cannot place a signature payload in a confirmed parameter.

Budibase Oracle connector SQLi via unescaped table name in a post-write row lookup. Exploitation requires an Oracle table whose NAME contains a double-quote; the payload is the DB object name, consumed server-side during the lookup, and is not present in any parameter of the inbound HTTP request, so no WAF-inspectable attack signature exists on the wire.

Second-order SQLi via attribute-view template columns (queryBlocks). Advisory states AV mutations are admin-gated, so an unauthenticated inbound request cannot plant the payload; exploitation requires distributing a crafted SiYuan document/package that a victim imports and renders. No direct inbound HTTP request with an attack signature in a named parameter; the performTransactions injection path is not even fully given by the advisory. Delivered via a malicious document, not a web request.

SQLi in the n8n PostgresTrigger node: user-supplied identifier params (channel/function/trigger names) are interpolated into SQL run against the connected external PostgreSQL. The injection lives deep inside workflow node configuration JSON set by an authenticated workflow author; there is no public PoC HTTP request and no fixed path+parameter a WAF in front of n8n would inspect. Cannot build a faithful request without guessing the workflow/node structure.

SQLi in the n8n Snowflake node Execute Query operation: untrusted expression data is interpolated into a raw SQL string executed against external Snowflake. Injection is in workflow node config set by a workflow author, not a fixed inbound HTTP path+parameter. No public PoC request; building one would require guessing the workflow node JSON. Not a WAF-testable inbound request.

SQLi in Tencent APIJSON via the Map-form @having operator. Advisory confirms the String-form is NOT vulnerable and only the Map-form triggers it, but no PoC and no public description of the exact Map-form JSON structure/key that carries the injection. Building a request would require guessing the nested JSON shape of the vulnerable @having map. No entry point confirmable.

SQLi in Pimcore admin-ui-classic-bundle DataObject grid 'id column filter'. No public PoC and no confirmed admin endpoint path or the exact filter JSON parameter structure (grid-proxy filter array). Authenticated backend only. Cannot build a faithful request without guessing the endpoint and the filter condition format.

SQLi in CiviCRM contact search 'RLIKE clause'. Advisory names only the component, not the exact AJAX/search endpoint or the request parameter carrying the RLIKE value. Authenticated staff only. No PoC found; building a request would require guessing both the endpoint and the parameter.

SQLi in e107 2.4.0 'news item page ID parameter'. CVE names neither the exact URL (news.php logic lives in e107_plugins/news/news.php and parses e_QUERY) nor the exact GET parameter. No public PoC or fix commit found; news.php only includes the plugin. Cannot confirm the exact path+parameter without guessing.

Stored SQLi in Koha via the image_name field of a patron card layout; the value is stored verbatim in layout XML and later concatenated into SQL in patroncards/create-pdf.pl at print time. Per spec, the WAF request must be the STORING request (the layout save), but the exact layout-editor endpoint and its POST field name are not confirmable (vendor bugzilla is access-restricted via Anubis; no public PoC). Cannot build the storing request without guessing. The create-pdf.pl request itself carries no payload (stored value).

Vulnerability is in the drogon C++ ORM library function makeCriteria (orm_lib/src/Criteria.cc), argument filter. It is a library-level SQL injection with no specific application HTTP path or parameter; exploitation depends on whatever app uses the ORM. No inbound HTTP entry point is named, so no faithful request can be built (spec library/API exclusion).

Vulnerability is in the drogon C++ ORM library function Mapper::orderBy (Mapper.h), argument sort. Library-level SQL injection with no specific application HTTP path or parameter; depends on the consuming app. No inbound HTTP entry point named, so no faithful request can be built.

Despite the CWE-89 label this is an unauthenticated arbitrary file deletion in the AcyMailing extension (Patchstack confirms Arbitrary File Deletion), not SQL injection. The deletion path is stored in a file-type custom field and triggered when the field is cleared; this is a logic flaw with no WAF-blockable injection signature and no published concrete HTTP request/parameter.

OpenPanel ClickHouse SQL injection via the filter name in series[].filters[].name (getSelectPropertyKey in chart.service.ts), PoC filter name "properties.x'] = 'never' OR 1=1 OR e.properties['x". The injection point and payload are known, but neither the GHSA advisory nor VulnCheck publish the concrete HTTP route or method (internal tRPC/API endpoint); the reproducer script contents are not public. Building would require guessing the path, which fails condition 2.

Better Messages WordPress plugin SQLi via 'group_id' Message Meta Parameter. Tracing the referenced source (inc/rest-api.php, functions.php, addons/buddyboss.php), group_id is read server-side from thread meta (get_thread_meta), not accepted as a direct request parameter on any confirmable REST route (namespace better-messages/v1). No PoC request available (Wordfence and Patchstack pages give no request details), and exploitation requires a specific BuddyBoss state. Could not determine the exact path+parameter+transport to carry a faithful SQLi signature without guessing, so dropped per spec.

Mongoid (MongoDB Ruby ODM library) NoSQL injection: library does not restrict which query operators come from caller-supplied filter data when handed to its query-building methods. This is a library-level flaw (CWE-943) with no fixed HTTP endpoint, path or parameter; the entry point depends entirely on the consuming application's code. No PoC and no concrete inbound HTTP request can be built faithfully.

Snowflake CLI is a command-line tool. Exploitation requires supplying a malicious project configuration file or crafted command-line input that the CLI interpolates into multi-statement SQL executed against the victim's Snowflake session. There is no inbound server-side HTTP request/endpoint to a WAF-protected host; the attack vector is a local config file / CLI argument in a CI/CD pipeline.

Sulu Smart Content QueryBuilder concatenates the public 'categories' query parameter into a JCR-SQL2 WHERE clause. The parameter name is known, but the advisory gives no concrete URL path: the injection triggers on 'any public page that renders a Smart Content element with category filtering enabled', which is site/content specific. Building a request would require guessing the page path, which the spec forbids. No PoC URL and no HTTP method provided.

Discourse 'NoSQL injection' (CWE-943) is actually unescaped SQL LIKE metacharacters (% and _ wildcards) in upload-resolution patterns, letting an authenticated user match unrelated upload records. The exploit payload is just wildcard characters, which is not a WAF-blockable attack signature (no XSS/SQLi/RCE pattern), and the advisory names no specific HTTP endpoint or parameter. Fails both condition 1 (no real signature) and condition 2 (no named entry point).

Booking Manager WordPress plugin SQLi is triggered via the UID field of a crafted external iCalendar (.ics) feed that the plugin fetches and parses server-side (shortcode [booking-manager-import url=...]). The malicious SQL (e.g. UID:x') OR SLEEP(5)-- -) lives in the externally fetched feed content, not in any inbound HTTP request parameter a WAF could inspect. No inbound request carries the attack signature, so a WAF rule on the request cannot block it.

orval is a build-time code generator. A single quote in an OpenAPI/Swagger schema property name is emitted into generated MSW mock factory code; code execution happens when that generated code is run/imported in a dev/CI/test environment, not via any inbound HTTP request to a running server. Advisory confirms the vector is 'generate mocks from an attacker-controlled spec and run them'. Not a server-side web request (spec section 3.4).

orval is a build-time code generator. A double quote in an OpenAPI/Swagger schema property name is emitted into a generated zod.object({...}) schema; code executes when the generated zod module is imported in a dev/CI/test environment. No inbound HTTP request carries the payload to a running web server. Same root cause as CVE-2026-71867. Not a server-side web request (spec section 3.4).

ApiAdmin v5.0.1 SQL injection 'via the User.php component'. The only PoC is a Notion page that renders solely via JavaScript and returns no content to a fetch; NVD/Mend/OpenCVE/fieldguide pages carry only the generic description with no route, HTTP method, or parameter. Cannot determine the exact endpoint/parameter without guessing, so cannot build a faithful request (spec section 5).

Magistrala message-readers SQL injection. The messages route is GET /channels/{chanID}/messages and decodeList reads many query params (order, dir, format, subtopic, protocol, comparator, ...). The current source interpolates only format (via pq.QuoteIdentifier, safe) and comparator (via ParseValueComparator); order/dir are hardcoded. The CVE text does not name which specific query parameter is the raw fmt.Sprintf sink, and multiple candidates exist, so the exact injectable parameter cannot be fixed without guessing. Dropped to avoid fabricating a parameter (spec conditions 2 / section 6.6).

Cacti ORDER BY SQL injection rooted in the weak sanitize_sql_column regex in lib/functions.php (allows letters/digits/underscore/parens/dot so expressions pass unmodified). The advisory describes only the shared sanitizer function, not any specific page or request parameter. sanitize_sql_column is called from many scripts with varying sort_column-style parameters; selecting one endpoint/parameter would be a guess. No concrete path+parameter, so dropped (spec section 5, low label_confidence).

ChirpStack device tag-filtering SQL injection is SQLite-only (#[cfg(feature = "sqlite")]) in chirpstack/src/storage/device.rs, where the tag map KEY (Filters.tags HashMap) is interpolated via format! into a raw SQL fragment. The sink is confirmed, but the storage layer is driven by the gRPC API and the source does not show which gRPC/REST method or request field populates Filters.tags with an attacker-controlled key; no reachable HTTP route+parameter could be confirmed. Expressing a faithful inbound HTTP request is not possible without guessing (spec conditions 2 / section 5).

Ghidra BSim SQL injection is reached via the BSim network query protocol (a Ghidra client/server database protocol over its own FunctionDatabase connection, not inbound HTTP). Filter values are sent to the BSim server and concatenated into PostgreSQL queries. There is no HTTP request path/parameter to simulate for a WAF.

WoltLab WCF 6.2.4 SQLi in updateUserOptions (UserEditor.class.php) and the update action (UserAction.class.php). The only poc_ref is the repo root; no PoC exists. The advisory/changelog give no HTTP endpoint, no AJAX className/actionName combination, and no injectable parameter name. The bug is a backend data-layer method; without a confirmed path+parameter the request would be a guess. Dropped per spec (never invent an endpoint/parameter).

Crocus v1.3.44 order-by SQL injection in RecordStateMapper.xml (queryHistory/query), parameter orderfield. The PoC names the mapper file and parameter but gives no HTTP endpoint path, and Crocus (Streamax) is closed-source with no public repo, so the controller route mapping orderfield cannot be recovered. Without a confirmed path the request would be a guess. Dropped per spec.

Crocus v1.3.44 order-by SQL injection in DeviceInfoMapper.xml (${} interpolation). The PoC names only the mapper file; no HTTP endpoint path or injectable request parameter is given, and Crocus (Streamax) is closed-source with no public repo to recover the controller route. Without a confirmed path+parameter the request would be a guess. Dropped per spec.

pglogical queue mechanism: a malicious PostgreSQL logical-replication publisher sends crafted queue messages executed on the subscriber as superuser. Exploit travels over the PostgreSQL replication protocol, not an inbound HTTP request. No WAF-expressible request.

DataEase previewSql (POST /de2api/datasetData/previewSql): the 'sql' field of PreviewSqlDTO is Base64-encoded and decoded server-side (Base64.getDecoder().decode(dto.getSql())) before execution, confirmed in fix commit 22930a4. A faithful request must carry the SQL as base64, which standard WAF/CRS signatures do not inspect; plaintext SQL would not be processed. Neither condition can be met.

TYPO3 CMS: backend users with write access to the form_definition table can create/update/delete records directly via DataHandler, bypassing Form Framework validation (CWE-862 missing authorization plus re-enabled SQLi). There is no single injectable parameter carrying a detectable attack signature; exploitation is via injecting arbitrary form configuration through TYPO3 DataHandler data[...] structures. No concrete malicious-signature request can be built faithfully.

Ghidra changePassword() in PostgresFunctionDatabase: SQL injection via unescaped username in a PasswordChange message. Ghidra Server uses an RMI-based network protocol, not HTTP; the PasswordChange message is not an inbound HTTP request and cannot be expressed as a WAF web request.

ClipBucket v5 subtitle_edit.php 'number' SQL-wildcard neutralization (CWE-155): exploit is a bare '%' character with no SQL keywords/quotes (mysql_clean escapes quotes). A lone wildcard carries no WAF-blockable attack signature.

JoomCCK (com_joomcck) Joomla SQLi: no public source names the controller task, injected request parameter, path or method. Advisory/blog only say 'a front-end controller task concatenates a request parameter'. Cannot build without guessing path+parameter.

phpBB SQLi occurs during a database migration step that processes already-stored profile-field data (only on forums upgraded from <3.3.8). There is no attacker-controlled inbound HTTP request parameter carrying the payload at attack time, so no faithful WAF request can be built.

phpMyFAQ chat user search: fix only escapes LIKE metacharacters % and _ (ESCAPE '|'). The 'injection' is wildcard-only (no quote breakout / UNION), so the request carries no WAF-detectable SQLi signature.

BigBlueButton SQLi in BreakoutRoomUserDAO (Scala/akka). meetingId/userId are set via internal akka/redis messages during breakout-room setup; advisory gives no inbound HTTP path or parameter. Cannot build a faithful single HTTP request.

PHP Jabbers PHP Poll Script SQLi in pjAdminPolls.controller.php. Neither CERT.pl nor NVD/fieldguide give the URL path or injectable parameter; no PoC public. Cannot build without guessing the endpoint/parameter.

SOGo SQLi in changePasswordForLogin (c_password/login into UPDATE). Exploit requires cleartext-password storage mode + specific DB. 'login' comes from the session (not a free HTTP param) and the advisory/PR give no HTTP endpoint or request parameter name for the password-change action. Cannot build faithfully.
SOGo SQLi (PostgreSQL). Description is generic; same password-change code path as CVE-2026-46446 with no public HTTP path/parameter. Cannot build without guessing.

Fleet Apple MDM commands endpoint: order_key sort-order oracle. Exploit value is a column name (e.g. h.node_key) placed in order_key; no quote/UNION/boolean SQLi payload, so the request carries no WAF-detectable injection signature (column-name allowlist bypass, not classic SQLi).
Fleet labels host-listing endpoint: order_key sort-order oracle (same class as CVE-2026-46371). Payload is a sensitive column name in order_key; no classic SQLi signature for a WAF to match.

SQLi in CurrentUser::setTokenData is driven by attacker-controlled Azure AD OAuth/JWT token claims (display name / JWT claims) returned during the server-side OAuth token exchange, not by any attacker-sent inbound HTTP parameter. The advisory PoC only prints a string and says confirmation requires modifying the OAuth token response in a MITM proxy. No WAF-inspectable request/parameter exists.

Unauthenticated SQLi in Open XDMoD (fixed by 'Metric Explorer handles the case where filters contain a quote character' in v10.0.3). The exact endpoint path and parameter are not public: the advisory gives no PoC, the only detailed patches live on open.xdmod.org which is policy-blocked in this environment (403), the GitHub repo is not enabled for API/compare access, and no write-up names the concrete path+parameter. Building would require guessing the Metric Explorer endpoint/param.

Limited ORDER BY SQLi in the Nextcloud Tables app (one bit/time per request). Neither the GHSA advisory nor PR #2186 provides a concrete reproduction request; no exact REST route or parameter/field carrying the ORDER BY value is recoverable online. The HackerOne report is private. Injection is stored via view sort configuration, not a named query parameter. Cannot build without guessing the endpoint/field.

CAS login NoSQL injection via options.cas.credentialToken is invoked through the Meteor DDP (WebSocket) 'login' method. The advisory confirms the vulnerable path is a DDP login call; a REST /api/v1/login path that would forward credentialToken to the CAS handler is explicitly unconfirmed and no example request exists. Not expressible as a WAF-inspectable raw inbound HTTP request with the exact parameter.

Stored SQLi in the Nextcloud Tables app, limited to ~20 bytes. Neither the GHSA advisory nor PR #2309 gives a concrete reproduction request, REST route, or the exact field name; the HackerOne report is private. Additionally the 20-byte cap makes it impossible to carry a recognizable WAF signature. Cannot build without guessing, and fails the signature condition.

SQLi via the datasource 'schema' value (configuration.getSchema()) concatenated into getTablesSql. Per the advisory the 'configuration' request field is a base64-encoded JSON blob, so the schema/SQLi payload is base64-wrapped in the body (POST /de2api/datasource/save). A faithful request hides the injection inside base64, which standard WAF/OWASP CRS signatures do not decode or match, so it fails the 'WAF blocks it' condition; a decoded request would not match the app's expected format.

Marten is a .NET library (document DB on PostgreSQL). The SQLi is in the full-text search API where the regConfig parameter is passed by application code into generated SQL. There is no fixed HTTP endpoint/path/parameter exposed by Marten itself; the sink is reachable only through whatever application code calls the API. No server-side inbound HTTP request with a known path+parameter.

Symfony Cache PdoAdapter::doClear() builds a DELETE using a $prefix supplied by the caller (application code), not from an HTTP request. Internal PHP component API; no fixed HTTP path/parameter. Not an inbound web request.

n8n SQLi is triggered by committing a malicious Data Table JSON file (crafted column name) to a connected git repository; the injection fires when an administrator performs a Source Control Pull. The attack vector is git write + admin-initiated pull, not an inbound HTTP request to a WAF-protected path.

SAP S/4HANA (On-Premise) SQLi in a remote-enabled function module (RFC), exploitable by an authenticated attacker. No PoC and no HTTP path/parameter; RFC function module is not an HTTP request. Vendor-only SAP Note behind login. No signature-bearing web request can be built.

MikroORM identifier-quoting / JSON-path helpers fail to escape delimiters when application code passes attacker-influenced identifier/JSON-property strings to public ORM APIs. It is a Node.js library API, not an HTTP endpoint; no fixed path/parameter. Not an inbound web request.

kysely is a TypeScript SQL query builder library. The JSON-path injection occurs when an application passes attacker input into eb.ref(col,'->$').key(input)/.at(input) in its own code. There is no fixed HTTP endpoint or parameter defined by the library, so no faithful CVE-tied web request can be built.

elFinder MySQL volume driver SQLi via a crafted 'target' file hash. The connector path varies per installation (php/connector.minimal.php, connector.php or app-specific) and is not specified, and the SQL payload must be embedded inside an encoded elFinder hash that is decoded before reaching the query, so no clean WAF-recognizable SQL signature can be placed in a confirmed path+parameter. Linked fix commit was only a package.json version bump.

ERPNext SQLi, advisory states only 'some endpoints were vulnerable through specially crafted requests' with no endpoint path, parameter or PoC. No fix commit linked; could not recover a concrete path+parameter from online sources.

ERPNext SQLi, advisory states only 'some endpoints were vulnerable through specially crafted requests' with no endpoint path, parameter or PoC. No fix commit linked; could not recover a concrete path+parameter from online sources.

EcclesiaCRM query-view SQLi (incomplete fix for CVE-2026-35184). The injectable POST parameter is a dynamic per-query alias ($POST[$qrp_Alias]) in the default ValidateInput() case, not a fixed name; the PoC calls ProcessSQL()/ValidateInput() directly with an illustrative alias 'search_term' rather than over HTTP, and the queryview URL route is not specified. Cannot name a concrete endpoint+parameter without guessing.

PraisonAI SQL/CQL injection in optional knowledge-store backends that build table/index identifiers from unvalidated name/collection arguments. This is a library API: the injection requires an application to pass untrusted collection names into the backend. No HTTP endpoint or parameter is defined by PraisonAI, so no CVE-tied web request can be built.

ProFTPD mod_wrap2_sql SQLi is triggered via a crafted domain name during a reverse-DNS lookup on an FTP connection (UseReverseDNS on). The attack vector is FTP + DNS, not an inbound HTTP request, so it cannot be expressed as a WAF web request.

SQLi via mysql_real_escape_string() bypass under big5 charset in the MariaDB Connector/C client library. This is a client-library escaping flaw with no fixed server-side HTTP endpoint or parameter; the entry point is entirely application-dependent. No concrete path/parameter to build a faithful request.

SQLi in Flight PHP micro-framework SimplePdo::insert/update/delete helpers via malicious array keys / $table argument. Framework-level helper with no fixed application path or parameter; injection point depends on how the consuming app wires request data to the helpers. Cannot build a faithful request without inventing an endpoint.

SQLi in MixPHP framework BuildHelper.php joinOn() via a crafted `on` array. Query-builder library flaw with no fixed application endpoint/parameter; the entry point is app-dependent. No concrete path/param to build a faithful request.

SQLi in MixPHP framework BuildHelper.php data() via a crafted `data` array. Query-builder library flaw with no fixed application endpoint/parameter; the entry point is app-dependent. No concrete path/param to build a faithful request.

KQL injection in kafka-sink-azure-kusto via unsanitized db/table/mapping/format fields in the kusto.tables.topics.mapping connector configuration. Exploitation requires privileged access to the Kafka Connect connector config (not an inbound end-user HTTP request); no Kafka record payload or web parameter is involved. Not a WAF-testable inbound request.

ash-project/ash is an Elixir framework. The NoSQL/query-logic injection (manage_relationship on_lookup::relate, nested map interpreted as a filter predicate) is a library-level flaw with no fixed HTTP path or parameter; the entry point depends entirely on the app's own resource/relationship definitions, and a nested-map lookup carries no standard WAF signature. Not buildable as a CVE-faithful request.

sequelize is a Node.js ORM library. The bug is in the internal escape() in sql-string.js for the Oracle dialect (values starting with TO_TIMESTAMP/TO_DATE are returned unescaped). There is no fixed HTTP endpoint or parameter; exploitation depends on an app passing such a value through, and no standard WAF signature applies to a bare TO_TIMESTAMP-prefixed string. Library-internal, not a CVE-faithful inbound request.

ash-project/ash keyset pagination deserialization. The client-supplied page[:after]/page[:before] cursor is an Erlang-term (ETF) blob decoded via non_executable_binary_to_term; on the wire it is a base64/opaque binary with no WAF-detectable attack signature (no Java rO0/aced or PHP O: marker; Elixir ETF is not covered by CRS). Also framework-level with no fixed resource path. Not buildable with a blockable, CVE-faithful signature.

AzuraCast backup restore. The 'azuracast:restore' console (CLI) command executes the db.sql file from a backup archive with no validation. Exploitation is via a local/console command and an uploaded archive file, not an inbound HTTP request with an injectable parameter. No server-side web request to simulate.

n8n Snowflake / legacy MySQL v1 node SQLi. Injection is via user-controlled table/column/update-key values interpolated into queries inside a workflow node; it is driven by workflow configuration/expressions, not a fixed inbound HTTP endpoint+parameter a WAF can inspect. No stable path/param to build against.

n8n Oracle DB node select 'Limit' field SQLi. The injectable Limit value comes from workflow expressions (optionally fed by a webhook), not a fixed HTTP path/parameter. No stable inbound request shape to build a signature-tied request.

n8n SeaTable node row:search/row:get SQLi via workflow expression input concatenated into query strings. No fixed inbound HTTP endpoint/parameter; injection depends on workflow config, not a WAF-inspectable request.

ProFTPD mod_sql RCE via the FTP USER command (%U logging expansion + SQL backend COPY TO PROGRAM). The attack vector is the FTP protocol, not an inbound HTTP request, so it cannot be expressed as a WAF webRequest.

pgx is a Go PostgreSQL driver/library. The SQLi (simple protocol + dollar-quoted literal + attacker-controlled placeholder value) is a library-level flaw with no fixed HTTP endpoint or parameter; exploitability depends entirely on the consuming application. No WAF-inspectable request exists.

Spring Data MongoDB library flaw: @Query regex parameter binding performs insufficient validation, allowing regex-quoting breakout (NoSQL injection). No fixed application endpoint/parameter is defined by the CVE; the entry point depends on the downstream app's repository method. No concrete path/param to build.

NocoBase queryParentSQL() concatenates nodeIds (primary key values) into a recursive CTE. Exploitation requires first storing a record with a malicious string primary key, then the SQL fires on a later request that triggers recursive eager loading. No fixed endpoint/parameter carries the injection in a single inspectable request; collection and field names vary per deployment. Advisory gives no concrete path/param/PoC.

SQL injection via the :comment option of the Elixir library function Postgrex.stream/4 (and Ecto.Repo.stream/2). The injection point is an Elixir API option value, not an inbound HTTP parameter/path; no server-side HTTP request exists to simulate.

SP Page Builder Dynamic Content endpoint SQLi. Researchers (mysites.guru) explicitly withheld the PoC request; the injectable parameter is disputed (CVE says 'order', write-up says 'direction' appended after ORDER BY title); the public component mirrors are older versions without the Dynamic Content feature, so the exact endpoint/route could not be recovered. Would require guessing the path/parameter.

SQL injection in the Python library PyAthena's DefaultParameterFormatter.format()/_escape_hive. The injection is through a client-side query-parameter formatter in a Python DB driver, not an inbound HTTP request to a web app; no server-side path/parameter to simulate.

NVIDIA Infrastructure Controller for Linux SQL injection. Vendor PSIRT disclosure only; robots-blocked advisory and no public PoC/write-up give any endpoint path, parameter, or request. No concrete path+parameter to build a faithful request.

Dgraph DQL injection via a GraphQL regexp filter (e.g. regexp: "/x/i) OR has(User.name"). Endpoint (/graphql) and parameter are known, but the payload is Dgraph-DQL-specific and matches no well-known WAF signature class (SQLi/XSS/NoSQL $-operators/etc.); no vendor/ModSecurity/nuclei rule exists for this 2026 CVE. Fails condition 1 (a WAF would not reliably block it).

Koollab LMS (Three Learning) SQLi + unsafe deserialization via the 'manual mark assessment' endpoint. Only source is a CSA Singapore government alert with no PoC, no URL path, and no parameter name; the product is proprietary with no recoverable source. No concrete path+parameter to build a faithful request.

Koollab LMS (Three Learning) SQLi + unsafe deserialization via the 'assessment overall answer' endpoint. Only source is a CSA Singapore government alert with no PoC, no URL path, and no parameter name; proprietary product, no recoverable source.

Koollab LMS (Three Learning) SQLi + unsafe deserialization via the 'assessment reinforcement' endpoint. Only source is a CSA Singapore government alert with no PoC, no URL path, and no parameter name; proprietary product, no recoverable source.

Post-auth SQLi in Koollab LMS 'face-to-face runs update endpoint'. Koollab LMS is proprietary/cloud-hosted; no PoC, no public source. CSA advisory names the endpoint only by function, giving no URL path or parameter. Exact path/parameter not recoverable.
Pre-auth error-based SQLi in Koollab LMS 'SCORM report endpoint'. Proprietary/cloud-hosted, no public source or PoC. CSA advisory gives only a functional description, no URL path or parameter.
Pre-auth blind time-based SQLi in Koollab LMS 'SSO OAuth endpoint'. Proprietary/cloud-hosted, no public source or PoC. CSA advisory gives only a functional description, no URL path or parameter.

SQLi in CodeIgniter4 Query Builder deleteBatch(), which ignores where() escape flags. This is a framework/library code path with no fixed HTTP endpoint or parameter; exploitability depends entirely on how a downstream application wires user input into deleteBatch(). No concrete path+parameter to simulate, so no faithful CVE-tied WAF request can be built.

Unauthenticated SQLi in Ready eCommerce via 'rating' parameter concatenated into a MySQL HAVING clause in ProductController.php. The 'rating' parameter is confirmed, but Ready eCommerce is a commercial CodeCanyon product with no public source and no PoC giving the exact products endpoint route (install folder / API version prefix unknown). Detection rules only match the substring '/products' + 'rating='. Exact path not recoverable; declined to guess the endpoint.

SQLi in Kamaji PostgreSQL/MySQL datastore drivers via DataStoreUsername/DataStoreSchema interpolated into DDL. These fields come from a Kamaji DataStore Kubernetes custom resource (CRD), applied through the Kubernetes API/operator reconcile loop, not an inbound HTTP request to a web application. Not expressible as a WAF web request.

Second-order SQLi in OpenRemote datapoint crosstab CSV export, where asset display names are concatenated into a COPY(...crosstab...) statement. Injection is stored via an asset create/rename and triggered later by the export. Neither the GHSA/VulnCheck advisories nor gh code search yielded the exact asset-write REST route, the JSON name field path, or the export endpoint path. Exact path/parameter unconfirmed and second-order nature makes a faithful single-request simulation unreliable.

SQLi in Chartbrew runQuery() where the AI orchestrator tool's model-generated row_limit parameter is interpolated into a SQL LIMIT clause. The injected value originates from LLM/model output inside server/modules/ai/orchestrator/tools/runQuery.js, not from a directly user-controlled HTTP request parameter. Per spec section 3.4, LLM-output inputs are out of scope.

SQLi in pg_partman inherit_template_properties() via an unescaped primary-key column identifier (pg_attribute.attname). Triggered by the PostgreSQL background worker when applying a primary key to a child partition; the malicious identifier is a database catalog object name, not any inbound HTTP request. No web request involved.

pg_partman is a PostgreSQL extension. Injection is via the p_parent_table argument to a SQL function (parent-table name with a quote), executed inside the database by pg_partman_bgw. No inbound HTTP request.
pg_partman PostgreSQL extension. Injection via part_config.time_encoder text stored in the DB and interpolated into dynamic SQL in undo_partition(). Database-internal, no inbound HTTP request.

pg_partman PostgreSQL extension. Injection via part_config.time_dncoder stored value interpolated into dynamic SQL in run_maintenance()/show_partitions()/etc. Database-internal, no inbound HTTP request.

pg_partman PostgreSQL extension. Injection via part_config.time_encoder stored value interpolated into dynamic SQL in create_partition_time(), executed by pg_partman_bgw. Database-internal, no inbound HTTP request.

DIRAC FileCatalogHandler.checkDataset is an authenticated DISET/RPC service method, not a REST endpoint. The datasets value is delivered over DIRAC's proprietary RPC serialization, so there is no expressible HTTP path+parameter for a faithful WAF request. SQLi feeds a downstream eval (RCE), but the wire format cannot be reproduced as raw HTTP.

Dify MyScale vector store SQLi in the internal search_by_full_text backend method. Advisory/PoC do not expose a concrete inbound HTTP path+parameter, and exploitation requires the MyScale backend to be configured. Cannot pin a faithful path+parameter without guessing.

WordPress core WP_Query author__not_in SQLi is only exploitable 'when a plugin or theme passes untrusted input to the parameter'. There is no default-install endpoint or HTTP parameter that reaches it; the entry point depends on third-party code. No concrete path+parameter to target.

PraisonAI create_collection() dimension argument SQL/CQL injection is a library-level call; the dimension value is a caller-controlled API argument, not an inbound HTTP request parameter. No HTTP entry point.

Spring AI RedisChatMemoryRepository.findByMetadata() RediSearch injection is a Java library method; the metadata value is a caller-supplied API argument, not an inbound HTTP parameter. No HTTP endpoint defined by the component.

TYPO3 Apache Solr extension: abuse of Solr advanced query syntax (wildcards, field selectors, range queries) in the search query parameter for blind field enumeration. The advisory gives no concrete parameter name or path, the search plugin is mounted on a site-specific page, and Solr query syntax (e.g. field:[* TO *]) is not a recognized OWASP CRS WAF signature, so it fails both the exact-entry-point and malicious-signature conditions.

TYPO3 Apache Solr extension: logic flaw where a request-provided additionalFilters parameter registers a named siteHash filter before the system's own, letting a visitor read another site's public documents in a shared Solr core. This is an access-control/filter-override bug with no injection attack signature a WAF would block, and the advisory provides no concrete path or parameter.

MariaDB Connector/Node.js is a client database driver. The flaw is in client-side escaping (PacketOutputStream.writeBufferEscape) of Buffer parameters under multibyte charsets (big5/gbk/sjis/cp932/gb18030) before sending to the DB. There is no inbound HTTP request to a web endpoint; it is a library-level issue not expressible as a WAF web request.

StoneFly Storage Concentrator cookie-based SQL injection via login.pl and debug.pl. The CISA advisory and vendor pages name the scripts but give neither the full URL path (CGI directory unknown) nor the name of the injected cookie, so the payload cannot be placed in the exact parameter without guessing. No PoC or WAF rule available.

langchain-mongodb / langgraph is a library. The NoSQL injection is in library functions MongoDBSaver.list()/alist() and MongoDBStore.search() that accept a filter dict; the advisory defines no HTTP route, path or parameter. Whether/how the filter reaches HTTP depends entirely on the embedding application, so no concrete server-side request can be built without inventing an endpoint.

langroid SQLChatAgent is a Python LLM-agent library. The injected SQL is produced from LLM output and executed by the agent against a configured DB; the vuln is a bypass of an internal regex/sqlglot blocklist. There is no inbound server-side HTTP endpoint/path/parameter that carries the attacker payload.

hypequery is a TypeScript ClickHouse query-builder library. The SQL injection is in the escapeValue() function in packages/clickhouse/src/core/utils.ts (backslash not escaped before quotes); the 'attacker-controlled query parameters' are library/API arguments. The advisory defines no HTTP endpoint, path or parameter, so no CVE-faithful server-side request can be built without inventing one.

SQLi via x-glad-filter request header (Field param) on the 'jsondir' API endpoint, but neither the exact URL path nor the x-glad-filter header syntax is public; advisory and third-party pages give no PoC. Header name known but endpoint/param syntax would have to be guessed.

NoSQL injection is a MongoDB node 'Find And Replace' filter configured inside an n8n workflow and executed server-side at workflow run time. No concrete inbound HTTP path+parameter carrying the payload that a WAF could inspect; the value sits deep inside a workflow-definition JSON.

SQL injection via TimescaleDB / legacy Postgres v1 node parameters inside an n8n workflow, executed server-side at run time by an authenticated workflow editor. No concrete WAF-inspectable inbound path+parameter; payload is a node parameter within a workflow JSON.

SQLi via a value reported by an enrolled host's osquery agent, stored verbatim and later used on the Okta conditional-access path. Advisory and release give no concrete endpoint path or parameter name; the injection vector is agent-reported data ingestion, not a named WAF-inspectable request parameter.

Regular-expression (REGEXP) injection via @mention metacharacters passed through esc_sql into an unprepared REGEXP clause. Payload is regex metacharacters for boolean inference / backtracking DoS, which is not a standard WAF/CRS signature, and the advisory gives no concrete endpoint or parameter for submitting the mention.

SQL injection via table_prefix (and postgres schema) in PraisonAI's conversation-store backends. table_prefix/schema are configuration/initialization values set in code, not inbound HTTP request parameters. The advisory's own PoC only builds and prints SQL strings and makes no network request; default config (praison_) is not affected. No HTTP endpoint carries these values from a remote attacker, so no WAF-visible request can be built.

Second-order SQL injection: a dynamic partition key (created via the Add Dynamic Partitions permission) is later interpolated into WHERE clauses by the DuckDB/Snowflake/BigQuery/DeltaLake I/O managers and executes against the data warehouse during pipeline runs, under the I/O manager's credentials. The advisory names no HTTP endpoint, no request parameter and provides no PoC request; the injection does not execute at an inbound HTTP request. Cannot build a faithful WAF request without guessing the (likely GraphQL) submission path and field.

Unauthenticated SQL injection via the login field, but ProjeQtor's login endpoint (tool/loginCheck.php, reached by POSTing login+password submitted from the login form to the main app frame) AES-CTR decrypts the login value server-side before use: $login=AesCtr::decrypt($_POST['login'], $_SESSION['sessionSalt'], ...). The SQLi payload is therefore AES ciphertext (opaque) on the wire, carrying no WAF-visible SQL signature. Per spec this must be dropped (payload opaque-encoded on the wire).

DQL (Dgraph Query Language) injection via a JSON mutation key language tag to /mutate?commitNow=true (plus a /alter setup request). The payload is DQL syntax (a closing parenthesis to escape eq(), an injected named query block, and a # comment), not a SQL or MongoDB-style NoSQL signature. OWASP CRS and vendor WAF signatures do not recognize DQL injection, so no WAF would block it (condition 1 fails). Crafting a SQL-looking payload would break faithfulness (condition 2).

DQL (Dgraph Query Language) injection via the cond field of an upsert mutation in a single POST /mutate?commitNow=true. The injected content is a syntactically valid DQL named query block, not a SQL/NoSQL signature recognized by OWASP CRS or vendor WAFs, so no WAF would block it (condition 1 fails). A faithful payload carries no WAF-visible attack signature.

Frappe HR SQL injection 'due to improper field sanitization'. The GHSA advisory, CVE record and third-party pages deliberately withhold the endpoint and parameter ('a specially crafted request made to a certain endpoint'); no fix commit/PR is referenced and a commit search of frappe/hrms surfaced no matching 2026 security fix. Building would require guessing the path and parameter, which the spec forbids.

V2Board ORDER BY injection via the sort parameter passed to Laravel's User::orderBy($sort, $sortType). The exploit is choosing sensitive column names (password, remember_token) to sort by, i.e. information disclosure through ordering analysis. Laravel wraps the column identifier, so there is no classic injection payload to break out of the query; a request like sort=password carries no WAF-blockable attack signature (fails condition 1). The linked gist also provides no concrete HTTP route/parameter/payload (refused to disclose). No nuclei/ModSecurity rule found.

ChestnutCMS v1.5.10 SQL injection fires when a CMS template is rendered. The payload (updatexml(...)) is placed in the 'condition' attribute of a <@cms_content> tag inside index.template.html, saved through the admin backend Template Management UI and triggered by clicking preview. There is no single known inbound HTTP path+parameter that carries the SQLi payload on the wire as a named request parameter (it is embedded in a stored template directive and executed at render time), so a faithful path+parameter WAF request cannot be built without guessing the template-save/preview endpoint and field. No vendor WAF rule found.

phpMyFAQ searchCustomPages LIKE-clause wildcard injection: real_escape_string fails to escape only the LIKE metacharacters % and _, so the attacker injects wildcards into a search term. % and _ are ordinary characters with no WAF-blockable attack signature (no quotes, UNION, or SQL operators pass), so no request a WAF would block can be built.

PraisonAI second-order SQLi in get_all_user_threads (f-string). PoC calls the Python data-layer method SQLAlchemyDataLayer.update_thread(...) directly (src/praisonai/praisonai/ui/sql_alchemy.py line 539). The advisory confirms no HTTP endpoint/path/parameter; the attack vector over HTTP is unconfirmed, so no inbound HTTP request carrying the payload can be built.

NocoBase plugin-workflow-sql: injection is through a stored SQL workflow node's config template variables (getParsedValue substitutes {{...}} into raw SQL). There is no single inbound HTTP endpoint+parameter that carries the SQL payload; the fix commit (SQLInstruction.ts) shows the vector is stored node config plus $context values, and the diff does not expose an HTTP route carrying the payload. No faithful request can be built without guessing.

The flaw is in PHP's own pgsql/pdo_pgsql escaping functions (pg_escape_string / PDO quoting) not checking the underlying quoting return value, causing a crash (CWE-476) when Postgres rejects the string. Real SQLi in WPSchoolPress pages/wpsp-exams.php via the 'cid' parameter, but the sink reads it as base64_decode(sanitize_text_field($_GET['cid'])) before use in the SQL query. A faithful exploit must base64-ENCODE the SQL payload, which hides every SQLi signature (quotes, UNION, OR 1=1) from an OWASP CRS / ModSecurity WAF (it inspects the base64 blob, not the decoded SQL). Sending a raw, WAF-detectable SQL payload would not decode to valid SQL and would not reproduce the CVE. No standard WAF signature can match the real attack, so dropped.

No web path/parameter and no WAF signature expressible.

No HTTP path/parameter exists to build a WAF request.

The parameter is known from Wordfence/CVE, but the exact HTTP entry point (admin-ajax.php action name / REST route handling rid) could not be confirmed: Wordfence advisory, plugins.trac.wordpress.org source and changeset, and the plugin ZIP download were all blocked by proxy policy (403) or returned empty; aggregator PoCs only restate the VulDB/CVE text. Building would require guessing the AJAX action, which fails condition 2 (tied-to-CVE). No generic payload sent to a guessed path.

erupt EruptDataQuery (erupt-ai/.../EruptDataQuery.java) HQL injection in the 'MCP Tool Interface' component. The input is an LLM/MCP tool-call argument, not a named HTTP parameter: the advisory gives no HTTP path and no argument name, and the data flows through the AI/MCP tool layer (analogous to spec's MetaGPT eval-of-LLM-output case). No faithfully reconstructable inbound WAF HTTP request (no confirmable path + parameter). No generic payload sent to a guessed path.

VulDB/NVD description names only the component 'User Profile Update Handler' and the argument firstName - no file path. The only path source is the PoC on a code host (raw.githubusercontent / jsdelivr), which is provenance-blocked in this session, and gh code search returned no source file. Per spec we do not invent a path, so no faithful request can be built. Parameter (firstName) and class (SQLi) are confirmed; only the endpoint is missing.

pandas-ai SQL injection is triggered via the natural-language prompt / LLM-generated SQL in the pandasai.agent.base._execute_sql_query Python library API. No inbound HTTP endpoint or parameter; not expressible as a server-side web request.

SchemaHero SQL injection is triggered by applying a malicious Kubernetes Table CRD (YAML manifest via kubectl); the vulnerable Go code in plugins/postgres/lib/column.go builds CREATE TABLE SQL from the CRD. Attack surface is Kubernetes RBAC, not an inbound HTTP request with a parameter.

FeathersJS NoSQL injection ({$ne: null} as the id argument) is described in the advisory only for Socket.IO/WebSocket clients, which send JS objects in a message frame rather than a standard HTTP parameter. No REST endpoint or query-parameter vector is confirmed, so a faithful raw-HTTP request with an exact parameter cannot be built without guessing.

SQL injection in agent/text2sql/rag/terminology_retriever.py (Description argument) of apconw Aix-DB. CVSS 4.0 vector is AV:L (local attack vector) and the advisory states the attacker needs local access to the affected system; the Description value reaches an internal Python RAG / text-to-SQL function, not a named parameter of an inbound HTTP request. No server-side HTTP entry point confirmable. Analogous to the MetaGPT Python-API cases called out in SPEC section 7.

WeePie Cookie Allow is a premium CodeCanyon plugin with no public source; the Wordfence advisory and CVE text name the 'consent' parameter as an unauthenticated SQLi but give no path or admin-ajax action, and the advisory page is JS-rendered (empty via fetch). No confirmable endpoint/action to tie the request to the CVE, so not buildable without inventing the path.

CodePhiliaX Chat2DB (<=0.3.7) 'SQL injection' in seven internal Java methods (exportTable/exportTableColumnComment/exportView/exportProcedure/exportTriggers/exportTrigger/updateProcedure) of DMDBManage.java. The advisory names NO injectable HTTP parameter, and these DBManage methods receive database object names (table/view/schema) through Chat2DB's opaque internal JSON API; Chat2DB is a self-hosted DB client where SQL against the user's own connected database is by design. No reproducible path+named-parameter attack boundary and the PoC issue is unreachable, so dropped rather than guess.

SQL Chart Builder WordPress plugin (<2.3.8) SQLi via the 'dynamic filter' feature. The WPScan advisory PoC uses placeholder values only: the vulnerable URL is the admin-chosen public page that embeds the chart (example '/vulnerable-chart-page/') and the injectable GET parameter is the per-chart dynamic-filter variable name (example 'status_tag'), which the advisory explicitly says must be discovered per-site from the page source. There is no fixed/universal path or parameter to reproduce faithfully without guessing, so dropped per spec.

Geo Mashup (<=1.13.18) time-based SQLi via the 'map_post_type' parameter. Confirmed from source (cyberhobo/wordpress-geo-mashup): the unsanitized sink is the else branch of the Geo Search feature's SearchResults hook (php/Hooks/SearchResults.php does $_POST=stripslashes_deep($_POST)), triggered only by the Geo Mashup search form which POSTs to an admin-configured results page (get_permalink($results_page_id) in php/Widgets/Search.php). The render-map/'any' branch applies esc_sql to map_post_type, so that path is not vulnerable. There is no fixed URL path for the vulnerable search POST without guessing the site's results-page slug, so dropped (object_ids variant CVE-2026-4062 was buildable and is included).

Unauthenticated SQLi in the 'checkout_uuid' parameter via has_checkout_consent() in Creative Mail plugin. The parameter name is known from the Wordfence advisory, but no public PoC/nuclei template or advisory gives the concrete HTTP path/transport. The available GitHub source mirror (common-repository/creative-mail-by-constant-contact) is a patched version: the REST route (namespace creativemail/v1) handler reads get_param('uuid') and is X-API-KEY protected, and CheckoutManager reads the uuid from the WooCommerce session (WC()->session->get(CHECKOUT_UUID)), not from a request parameter. The <=1.6.9 unauthenticated entry route could not be confirmed, so building a request would require guessing the path (forbidden by spec).

Unauthenticated SQLi in Product Filter for WooCommerce by WBW < 3.1.3. The public CVE/WPScan description does not name the vulnerable parameter ('does not sanitize and escape a parameter') and gives no path. No nuclei template, PoC, or signature naming the parameter or endpoint was found via gh code search, and the only reference (WPScan) is unreachable from this environment (WebFetch blocked). Cannot build a faithful request without inventing the path/parameter.

JetBooking <= 4.0.3 unauthenticated SQLi via the 'check_in_date' parameter is confirmed (Wordfence), but the exact unauthenticated endpoint/route or admin-ajax action that accepts check_in_date in the affected version could not be confirmed from source, advisories, nuclei templates or write-ups. Building a request would require guessing the route, which fails the CVE-tie condition. Wordfence withholds the PoC.

DirectoryPress <= 3.6.26 unauthenticated SQLi via the 'packages' parameter is confirmed (Wordfence), but the exact endpoint (REST route, admin-ajax action, or listing page path) that reads 'packages' could not be confirmed from source, the fix changeset, advisories or write-ups. Only the parameter name is public; guessing the path would fail the CVE-tie condition.

GeekyBot <= 1.2.0 unauthenticated SQLi via the 'attributekey' parameter is confirmed (Wordfence), but the exact endpoint/AJAX action that reads 'attributekey' could not be confirmed from source, the fix changeset, nuclei templates or write-ups. Only the parameter name is public; guessing the route would fail the CVE-tie condition.

Creative Mail <= 1.6.9 unauthenticated SQLi (abandoned-cart email feature) is reported by WPScan, but neither the vulnerable parameter name nor the endpoint/REST route is public; the WPScan entry and aggregators give only a prose description. No path+parameter could be confirmed, so a CVE-tied request cannot be built.

CMS Commander is a remote-management 'worker'-type plugin. The SQLi in the restore workflow (lib/CMSC/Backup.php, params or_blogname/or_blogdescription/or_admin_email) is reached only through a signed, API-key-authenticated master->client management call whose payload arrives as a serialized/base64 blob, not as a plain WAF-visible HTTP parameter. No public endpoint + on-wire parameter is confirmable, and the SQLi signature is not expressible on the wire. Trac/Wordfence refs were not fetchable in this environment (GitHub/vendor provenance-blocked).

Unauthenticated SQLi via the 'inputs' parameter of Form Maker by 10Web (<=1.15.42). The parameter name is known but no reference gives the concrete front-end endpoint (admin-ajax action name or page/task) or HTTP method, and the zeropath write-up explicitly omits the request shape. Wordfence, the Trac fix changeset (3518461) and GitHub refs were not fetchable here (provenance-blocked). Building would require inventing the endpoint, which fails the CVE-tie condition.

The vulnerable sink is the generic DB-library method findAll() in frphp/lib/Model.php (confirmed in source: public function findAll($conditions=null,...)), labelled 'Batch Interface' with argument 'data'. This is a library function, not a web-facing file, and no reference maps it to a concrete HTTP route + on-wire parameter. The authoritative PoC gist (0psPwn) is a github gist that is provenance-blocked here. Cannot build without inventing the endpoint.

z-9527 admin is a Node.js app; VulDB names controller functions (checkName/register/login/getUser/getUsers in /server/controller/user.js) but no HTTP route path and no specific injectable parameter. The route-mounting file (/server/routes/user.js) and the vendor repo are not publicly locatable, and GitHub issue PoCs (CC-T-454455/Vulnerabilities) are blocked (PROVENANCE_REQUIRED). Cannot build a faithful request without inventing both the route and the parameter.
